Commit ff936a04e5f2 (""bpf: fix cb access in socket filter programs"")
added a fix for socket filter programs such that in i) AF_PACKET the
20 bytes of skb->cb[] area gets zeroed before use in order to not leak
data
column2: and ii) socket filter programs attached to TCP/UDP sockets need

column1: to save/restore these 20 bytes since they are also used by protocol
layers at that time.
The problem is that bpf_prog_run_save_cb() and bpf_prog_run_clear_cb()
only look at the actual attached program to determine whether to zero
or save/restore the skb->cb[] parts. There can be cases where the
actual attached program does not access the skb->cb[]
tail calls into another program which does access this area. In such
a case
column2: the zero or save/restore is currently not performed.

column1: Since the programs we tail call into are unknown at verification time
and can dynamically change
column2: we need to assume that whenever the attached

column1: program performs a tail call
column2: that later programs could access the

column1: skb->cb[]
column2: and therefore we need to always set cb_access to 1.
